title: The Last Surrender
logline: A decorated veteran refuses to disarm their aging command ship, and a fearful bureaucrat hires a pilot to quietly sink it before the navy is forced to.

roles.description: Proud, deeply confused, and convinced the war is still happening.
Sweating through their uniform, desperate to avoid a PR disaster.
A massive, heavily armed relic of a forgotten war.
A small supply ship run by the captain's old crew.
The official fleet, embarrassed by the standoff.

public_situation: The {role:veteran_flagship} has been ordered to stand down and scrap its weapons, but it remains heavily armed in orbit, refusing all hails.
private_truth: The captain isn't rebellious; they are suffering from severe memory loss and believe the war is still going on. The bureaucrat wants to sink them to avoid a public tribunal.

beats.public_change: The flagship powers up its main battery, targeting an empty patch of space.

missions.reason: The bureaucrat needs the pilot to scan the flagship's engines to see if they are capable of jumping away.
missions.private_fact: The scan reveals the engines have been quietly rigged to overload if they try to jump.

beats.public_change: A small supply ship attempts to run the navy's blockade to reach the flagship.

missions.reason: The bureaucrat asks the pilot to destroy the loyalists trying to resupply the rogue captain.
missions.private_fact: The loyalists are actually just delivering desperately needed medical supplies for the captain's condition.

beats.public_change: The navy issues a final ultimatum: surrender in one hour or be destroyed.

missions.reason: The pilot is hired to attack the flagship directly to force its automated systems to shut down.
missions.private_fact: The captain hails the pilot, confused and terrified, offering their entire pension if the pilot will escort them back to the 'front lines'.

resolutions.summary: The captain dies, and the navy avoids an embarrassing public trial. The bureaucrat is promoted for their quiet handling of the crisis.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot blew a legendary war hero out of the sky to cover up the navy's mess.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot takes the captain's offer and escorts them away.
resolutions.summary: The flagship jumps away to parts unknown. The navy is humiliated, and the bureaucrat is blamed for the disaster.
The navy boards the flagship and arrests the captain. The bureaucrat's cover-up fails.

loose_threads.detail: The flagship's engines were rigged to overload using a signature known to belong to a notorious corporate hacker collective.
The bureaucrat pays the pilot using an unmarked credit line drawn from an offshore shell corporation.

radio_hooks: Standoff continues at {role:memorial_dock} as {role:veteran_flagship} refuses to disarm.

voice_direction.stubborn_captain: Authoritative, booming, but prone to sudden lapses in memory.
voice_direction.anxious_bureaucrat: Fast, quiet, constantly looking over their shoulder.
